title: CRM Training Guide
intro: Step-by-step GoHighLevel training. New team members can work through the lessons in order; experienced users can search for a specific task.

sections.name: Core CRM
sections.blurb: The main areas of the CRM you will use every day.

sections.name: Settings & Configuration
sections.blurb: Set up your profile, calendars and data fields.

sections.name: Additional Tools
sections.blurb: Apps and reporting beyond the core workspace.

lessons.title: Navigating the Launchpad
lessons.description: Use the Launchpad setup guide to see which core GoHighLevel features are set up in your account, which still need attention, and where to find built-in tutorials.
whatYouWillLearn: Open the Launchpad from the left sidebar
Read the setup progress bar and task completion percentages
Switch between the setup categories
Expand a setup task and open its tutorial video

sop.heading: Open the Launchpad
steps: In the left sidebar, click **Launchpad**.
Review the **Setup Guide**. The progress bar at the top shows how much of the selected category is complete.

sop.heading: Review setup tasks
steps: Click **Foundational setup** to see the core tasks, such as **Create a new contact**, **Import and engage with all your contacts instantly** and **Generate new leads with a high-converting funnel**.
Check the percentage beside each task. A green check with **100%** means the task is complete; **0%** means it has not been started.
Click the arrow on the right of a task to expand it. Where a video is available, play it under **Watch the Tutorial**.
Scroll down to see the remaining tasks in the category, such as **Book more appointments with automated scheduling** and **Accelerate deal closures with a streamlined sales pipeline**.

sop.heading: Switch categories
steps: Click each category in the **Setup Guide** menu to view its tasks: **Marketing & lead generation**, **Sales & conversations**, **Website & monetization** and **Ecommerce**.
Note the progress bar updates to show completion for the selected category.

importantNotes: Not every Launchpad task is required. Use it to confirm the key items are connected and to see what GoHighLevel can do, rather than completing every item.

screenshots.caption: Foundational setup tasks with completion percentages and an expanded task showing Watch the Tutorial.

lessons.title: Understanding the Dashboard
lessons.description: Switch between dashboards, read the default GoHighLevel dashboard widgets, customize a dashboard and change the reporting date range.
whatYouWillLearn: Switch between the default dashboard and custom dashboards
Read the opportunity, conversion, funnel, task and reporting widgets
Recognize why a widget may show no data or a connection error
Add, resize, duplicate or delete widgets in edit mode
Change the date range and compare against a previous period

sop.heading: Switch dashboards
steps: In the left sidebar, click **Dashboard**.

Click the dashboard selector at the top left (it shows the current dashboard name, for example **Dashboard**) and choose a dashboard from the **Shared with me** list. Use **Search for a dashboard** if the list is long.
To start a new dashboard, click **New** next to the selector.

sop.heading: Read the default dashboard
steps: **Opportunity status** shows how your opportunities are distributed across open, won and lost. Use the **All pipelines** drop-down on the widget to filter by pipeline.
**Opportunity value** shows **Total revenue**, and **Conversion rate** shows the win rate with **Won revenue** below it.
**Funnel** and **Stages distribution** show how opportunities are spread across stages. Select the pipeline from the drop-down on each widget.

**Tasks** lists tasks you can filter by status (**Pending**), sort order (**Due date (ASC)**) and user. **Manual actions** shows pending **Phone** and **SMS** actions; click **Go to manual actions** to work them.

Scroll down for **Lead source report**, **Google Business Profile**, **Facebook Ads report**, **Google Ads report**, **Email health report**, **Google Analytics count**, **Google Analytics chart** and **Sales efficiency**.

sop.heading: Review a custom dashboard
steps: Open the dashboard selector and choose a custom dashboard built for your account.
Scroll through its sections. In the example shown, widgets are grouped under **Top of Funnel**, **Consults & Show Rate**, **Conversion & Revenue** and **Health**.

sop.heading: Customize a dashboard
steps: Click **Edit dashboard**. The dashboard enters **Edit mode** and the **Add new widget** panel opens with the **Widgets**, **Elements**, **Themes** and **Custom metrics** tabs.
Find a widget with **Search widgets**, filter by **Chart type**, or expand a category such as **Contacts**, **Opportunities** or **Calls**.
Drag the bottom-right corner of a card to resize it, or drag a card to move it.
To remove a widget you do not use, click the three-dot icon next to its title and select **Delete**. The same menu offers **Edit** and **Duplicate**.
Click **Save changes** to keep your edits, or **Cancel** to discard them.

sop.heading: Change the date range
steps: Click the date range button at the top right (default **Last 30 days**).
Choose a preset under **Select date range**, or click a start and end date on the calendar to set **From** and **To**.
To compare periods, open **Comparison date range** and choose an option such as **Previous 31 days** or **Year before** (default **No comparison**).
Click **Apply**. The button then shows the selected date range.

importantNotes: Revenue, won value and conversion widgets only populate when opportunities are updated to won or lost with a monetary value. If numbers look wrong, check how opportunities are being updated.
If **Funnel** or **Stages distribution** shows **Funnel is disabled for this pipeline**, the pipeline must be enabled for these charts in Opportunities.

Reports showing **Connection expired. Reconnect to continue.** need their integration (Google Analytics, Facebook Ads, Google Ads) reconnected before data appears. **Email health report** requires at least 500 emails sent in the last 30 days.

lessons.title: Using Conversations
lessons.description: Learn the layout of the Conversations tab so you can check unread messages, find and organize conversations, view contact details alongside a thread, and know what each Conversations sub-tab is for.
whatYouWillLearn: The three panels of the Conversations view
How to check, filter, and clear unread messages
How to star important conversations
How to switch between My inbox, Team inbox, and Internal chat and search conversations
What Manual Actions, Snippets, Trigger Links, Analytics, and Settings are used for

sop.heading: Open Conversations
steps: In the left menu, click **Conversations**. The **Conversations** sub-tab opens with three panels: the conversation list on the left, the message thread and history in the center, and the selected contact's details on the right.

sop.heading: Check and organize messages
steps: Start on the **Unread** tab of the inbox to check for any unread messages.
After reading them, check **Select all** to select every conversation in the list and mark them as read.
Use the **All**, **Recent**, and **Starred** tabs to switch which conversations are listed.

To star a conversation you need to return to (for example, an important conversation or a client), check the box next to the contact's name and choose the star option from the dropdown that appears. Starred conversations appear under **Starred**.

sop.heading: Reply and view contact details
steps: Click a conversation to open it in the center panel. Reply to texts and messages from this panel.

Use the icons on the right edge of the screen to open the contact's sections without leaving the conversation, including **Activity**, **Associations**, **Tasks**, and **Agent Logs**, as well as opportunities, notes, appointments, documents, and payments.

sop.heading: Switch inboxes and search
steps: Use the icons to the left of the conversation list to switch between **My inbox**, **Team inbox**, and **Internal chat**. **Internal chat** is for messages between team members.

Click the expand arrow on the left edge of the conversation list to open the full inbox menu. Under **My inbox**, choose **All**, **Assigned to me**, or **Followed by me** to see conversations assigned to you or that you follow.
Type in the **Search** box at the top of that menu (minimum 3 characters) to find any conversation.

sop.heading: Other Conversations tabs
steps: Click **Manual Actions** to see calls and SMS messages that a workflow has queued for you to complete manually. Filter with **Workflows**, **Select Workflow**, and **Select Assignee**, and click **Let's Start** to work through the queued actions.

Click **Snippets** to manage saved messages you can insert into a conversation, such as a reply to a common objection or an email with your business information. Click **New Snippet** to create one or **New Folder** to organize them.

Click **Trigger Links** to manage tracked links (for example, a link to your calendar) used inside SMS messages and emails. Each click on the link records data about the contact. Click **Add Link** to create one and use the **Analyze** tab to review clicks.
Click **Analytics** to view **SLA performance**, which tracks response times once SLA settings are turned on with **Turn on SLA settings**.
Click **Settings** to define response time targets under **SLA Settings** using **Set SLA**.

importantNotes: Sending texts and emails, and the full detail of each contact section, are covered in the Contacts lesson.

screenshots.caption: The Conversations view: inbox list with Unread, All, Recent, and Starred tabs on the left, the message panel in the center, and the contact details panel with section icons on the right.
The expanded inbox menu with My inbox (All, Assigned to me, Followed by me), Team inbox, Internal chat, Views, and the Search box.
The Snippets tab with the New Folder and New Snippet buttons.

lessons.title: Using the Calendar
lessons.description: Learn how to view booked appointments by calendar or user, book an appointment correctly from the Calendars tab, and find where to connect your personal calendar.
whatYouWillLearn: How to filter the calendar by calendar and by user to see who is booked
How to open the Book appointment window
Why choosing the right calendar and team member matters
How timezones work when picking a slot and how to check the contact's local time
How to book a custom or recurring time
Where to set appointment status and where to connect your personal calendar

sop.heading: View who is booked
steps: In the left menu, click **Calendars**. The **Calendar view** tab opens with the **Manage view** panel on the right.
Under **Filters**, expand **Calendars** and check one or more calendars to see the appointments booked in them. This is useful when booking for someone else and checking availability.
Expand **Users** and check one or more users to show only the appointments booked for them.

sop.heading: Book an appointment
steps: Click **New** at the top right, or click the time slot on the calendar where you want the meeting. The **Book appointment** window opens on the **Appointment** tab. The same window opens wherever you book a meeting in GoHighLevel, including from a contact.

Under **Calendar**, select the correct calendar first (for example, a discovery call, consultation, or personal calendar). Booking in the wrong calendar can send the contact the wrong automations, texts, and reminders, or book the wrong person.
**Appointment title** defaults to **{{contact.name}}**. Leave it as is or change it, and click **Add description** if you want to add details.
Under **Team member**, select the team member who will actually take the call.
Under **Date & time**, confirm the timezone shown under **Showing slots in this timezone: (Account timezone)** is correct. The slots listed are in this timezone, not the contact's.
On the **Default** tab, choose a **Date** and a **Slot** from the available intervals.
If the time you need is not listed, click **Custom** and set the **Start time** and **End time**. Check **Recurring event** if the meeting repeats.
Under **Select Contact**, search by name, email, or phone and select the contact. Check the contact's local time shown under their name to confirm the appointment time is correct for them.
At the bottom, set **Status** to **Confirmed** or **Unconfirmed**.
Click **Book appointment** to save the appointment.

sop.heading: Update status after the call
steps: After the call, open the appointment and update its status if the contact did not show or the appointment was cancelled, so reporting reflects the correct outcome.

sop.heading: Connect your personal calendar
steps: Click **Settings** at the bottom of the left menu, then click **My Profile**.

Click **Calendar**, and on the **Calendars** tab under **Connected calendars**, click **Add new** to connect Google Calendar or the calendar you use. Your appointments then show there and your busy times are blocked off.

importantNotes: The timezone in the Book appointment window is your account timezone. Always compare against the contact's local time before booking. For example, a contact in Central time sees a 10:00 AM Eastern slot as 9:00 AM.
Connecting your calendar is covered step by step in a separate lesson.

screenshots.caption: The Book appointment window: Calendar, Appointment title, Team member, and Date & time with the account timezone and Default and Custom tabs.
After selecting a contact, the contact's local time appears under their name on the right.
Settings, My Profile, Calendar: the Connected calendars section with the Add new button.

lessons.title: Managing Contacts
lessons.description: Open a contact record and work it end to end: set ownership, review and update fields, manage Do Not Disturb, send messages, and log tasks, notes, and appointments from one screen.
whatYouWillLearn: Open a contact record and navigate its three panels
Assign an owner and add followers to a contact
Find and update contact, general, and custom fields
Turn Do Not Disturb on or off for all or individual channels
Review a contact's opportunities, workflows, and client portal access
Send an email or text with snippets, custom values, and scheduling options
Add tasks, notes, and appointments and review documents, payments, and agent logs

sop.heading: Open a contact record
steps: In the left sidebar, click **Contacts**. The **Smart Lists** tab opens and shows the contact list.

Click a contact's name to open **Contact Details**. The record has three areas: contact details on the left, **Conversations** in the middle, and a detail panel on the right that changes based on the icon you select in the icon bar on the far right.

sop.heading: Set owner and followers
steps: Under **Owner**, click the dropdown (shows **Unassigned** when no one is assigned) and select the user responsible for the contact.
Under **Followers**, click the dropdown and add any user who is helping work the contact but is not the owner.

sop.heading: Review and update contact fields
steps: Click the **All fields** tab. To find a specific field quickly, type in **Search fields and folders**.

Expand each folder to review or update values: **Contact** (**First name**, **Last name**, **Email**, **Phone**, **Date of birth**, **Contact source**, **Contact type**), **General Info** (**Business name**, **Street address**, **City**, **Country**, **State**, **Postal code**, **Website**, **Time zone**), and **Additional Info** (custom fields created for the account). Click into a field to edit its value.

sop.heading: Set Do Not Disturb (DND)
steps: Click the **DND** tab. Check **DND All Channels** to block all channels, or check only the channels to block: **Email**, **Text Messages**, **Calls & voicemail**, or **Inbound Calls and SMS**.
To remove DND, uncheck the box for that channel or for **DND All Channels**.

sop.heading: Review Actions
steps: Click the **Actions** tab. Under **Opportunities**, click **+ Add** to create a new opportunity, or click an existing opportunity card to open its edit window. Click **Load More** to see additional opportunities.
Expand **Workflows** to see the contact's **Active workflows** and **Past workflows**. Use this as an audit log to confirm which automations a contact has gone through.
Expand **Client portal** to view the contact's **Offers** and **Community groups**.

sop.heading: Send a message
steps: In the **Conversations** area, click **Type a message** to open the composer, then select the channel from the dropdown at the top left of the composer (for example, **Email**). Available channels depend on the contact's details and the channels connected to the account.
Confirm the **From** address and **From Name** and change them if needed. For email, enter a **Subject**, then type your message. Text messages have no subject line.

Use the toolbar at the bottom of the composer as needed: text formatting, emoji, **Insert Link**, file attachment, **Snippets**, trigger links, **Custom Values** (for example, **Contact** > **Full Name** inserts {{contact.name}}), **Request Payment**, and image. Click the trash icon to clear the message.
Click the arrow next to the send button and choose **Send**, **Send Later**, or **AI Schedule**.

sop.heading: Use the right-side panel
steps: Click the **Activity** icon to see page visits, form submissions, appointments, and calls for the contact. Review this before calling so you know the contact's recent actions.
Click the **Associations** icon. Under **Companies**, click **Create new** or **Link existing** to connect the contact to a company record.
Click the **Opportunities** icon to see the contact's opportunities and their pipeline stages, or click **+ Add** to create one.

Click the **Tasks** icon, then **Add task**. Enter a **Title**, add a description or click **Remove description**, set the **Due date and time**, optionally turn on **Setup recurring tasks**, select a user under **Assign to**, and click **Create**.

Click the **Notes** icon, then **Add note**. Enter a **Title** that summarizes the note and the **Description** (required). Optionally pick a **Color** or click **Upload file** to attach files, then click **Save**.

Click the **Appointments** icon to see **Upcoming** and **Past** appointments. To book one, click **+ Add** > **Meetings**, complete the **Book appointment** window (**Calendar**, **Appointment title**, **Team member**, **Date & time**, **Meeting location**, **Status**), and click **Book appointment**.

Click the **Documents** icon to view agreements and other documents (**All**, **Internal**, **Sent**, **Received**), the **Payments** icon to view **Transactions**, **Subscriptions**, **Invoices**, and **Estimates**, and the **Agent Logs** icon to view actions logged by an AI agent for this contact.

importantNotes: A contact who replies STOP to a text, or unsubscribes from an email campaign, is marked DND automatically. You only need to uncheck DND manually if the contact later asks to be contacted again.

screenshots.caption: The DND tab: check DND All Channels or individual channels such as Email or Text Messages.
The Actions tab with Opportunities, Workflows (Active and Past), and Client portal (Offers and Community groups) expanded.
The Add task panel opened from the Tasks icon in the right icon bar: Title, description, Due date and time, Assign to, then Create.

lessons.title: Managing Opportunities & Pipelines
lessons.description: Work opportunities on the pipeline board: switch pipelines, move cards through stages, use card quick actions, and edit opportunity details such as stage, status, and value.
whatYouWillLearn: Open the Opportunities board and switch between pipelines
Move opportunities between stages with drag and drop
Mark an opportunity as Won, Lost, or Abandoned
Use the quick action icons on an opportunity card
Tell the difference between the opportunity card and the contact record
Edit pipeline, stage, status, value, and owner in the opportunity window
Delete an opportunity that should not be in the pipeline

sop.heading: Open the pipeline board
steps: In the left sidebar, click **Opportunities**. The **Opportunities** tab opens with opportunity cards arranged in stage columns.
Click the pipeline dropdown at the top left (for example **Lead Pipeline**) and select the pipeline you want to work in.

Read the board from left to right. The first column (for example **New Lead**) holds the newest, most open opportunities; columns further right hold opportunities closer to a decision. Scroll right to see later stages. Each column header shows the opportunity count and total value.

sop.heading: Move opportunities through stages
steps: Drag an opportunity card and drop it into the stage column it now belongs in.

To close out an opportunity, start dragging the card. Drop zones appear at the bottom of the screen: drop it on **Won** if the deal closed and payment was collected, or on **LOST** if the lead is not interested or did not close. **ABANDONED** is also available.

sop.heading: Use card quick actions
steps: Use the icons along the bottom of a card to act without opening the contact. Hover to see each label: **Call**, conversation, **Add tags**, **Add note**, **Add task**, and **Add an appointment**.

To open the full contact record, click the contact name at the top of the card. The **Contact Details** page opens in **Contacts**. To return to the board, click **Opportunities** in the left sidebar (the back arrow on the contact record goes to the Contacts list, not the board).

sop.heading: Edit opportunity details
steps: Click anywhere on the card outside the contact name. The **Edit** window opens on **Opportunity details**.
To move the opportunity, select a different **Pipeline** and then the **Stage** it belongs in.
Set **Status** to **Open**, **Lost**, **Won**, or **Abandon**.
When a deal is won, enter the closed amount in **Value**.
Confirm or set **Owner** and **Followers**, and fill in **Source**, **Expected Close Date**, and **Tags** as needed.
Use the menu on the left of the window (**Source**, **Revenue**, **Outcome**, **Dates**, **Tasks**, **Notes**, **Payments**, and others) to view additional sections.
Click **Update** to save your changes, or close the window with the **X** to leave without saving.

sop.heading: Delete an opportunity
steps: If an opportunity should not be in the pipeline, open it and click the red trash icon at the bottom of the **Edit** window, next to **Cancel**.

importantNotes: If you mark an opportunity as Won without entering its Value, the amount will not appear in dashboard reporting. Always update Value when closing a deal.
Clicking the contact name opens the contact record; clicking elsewhere on the card opens the opportunity. These are two different records.
After you add notes, tasks, or appointments from a card, the card shows a count on that icon so you can see at a glance which opportunities have activity.

screenshots.caption: While dragging a card, the LOST, ABANDONED, and Won drop zones appear along the bottom of the board.
Quick action icons on an opportunity card. Hover an icon to see its label, such as Add an appointment.
The opportunity window: Pipeline, Stage, Status, Value, Owner, Source, and the Update and delete buttons.

lessons.title: Using Payments
lessons.description: Find your way around the Payments area: connect a payment provider, locate invoices, documents, orders, and subscriptions, and understand how products and payment links fit together.
whatYouWillLearn: Connect a payment provider, accounting software, and payment permissions
Find invoices, estimates, and invoice templates
Create and manage documents and contracts for signature
Locate orders, abandoned checkouts, and subscriptions
Create a product and use it in a payment link
Find coupons, gift cards, and payment integrations

sop.heading: Connect a payment provider
steps: In the left sidebar, click **Payments**. The **Invoices** page opens under **Invoices & Estimates**.

In the **Get started with payments** panel, click **Connect your payment provider** to see supported providers (Stripe, NMI, Authorize.net, PayPal, Square, Mercado Pago, and custom providers). You can also click **Integrate Payment Gateway** on the Invoices page.
Click **Connect your accounting** to connect QuickBooks.
Click **Control who can see your payments** to set which team members can view payments.

sop.heading: Invoices, estimates, documents, and contracts
steps: Open the **Invoices & Estimates** dropdown to reach **All Invoices**, **Recurring Invoices**, **Templates**, **Estimates**, and **Accounting Sync**. The Invoices page shows totals for draft, due, received, and overdue invoices.
Open the **Documents & Contracts** dropdown and choose **All Documents & Contracts** to create documents and contracts and send them for signature, or **Templates** to build reusable templates.

sop.heading: Orders and subscriptions
steps: Open the **Orders** dropdown to view **Orders** and **Abandoned Checkouts** for product sales.
Click **Subscriptions** to view recurring payments.

sop.heading: Create a product and payment link
steps: Make sure a payment provider is connected first.
Click **Products**, then click **Create Product**. You can also use **Import as CSV** or **Import from Stripe**.
Click **Payment Links**, then click **Create New Payment Link** (or **Create Link**).
In the link editor, under **Product**, click **Select a product** and choose the product. Set **Options** and **Advanced Options** as needed, then click **Save**.

sop.heading: Coupons, gift cards, and integrations
steps: Click **Coupons** and then **Create Coupon** to create discounts, or click **Gift Cards** to manage gift cards.
Click **Integrations** to see all payment providers, each with a **Connect** button. Use **Configure providers** to manage connected providers.

importantNotes: You need at least one connected payment gateway before you can receive payments.

screenshots.caption: The Get started with payments panel: connect a payment provider, connect accounting, and control who can see payments.
The payment link editor. Choose the product under Product, set options on the left, and click Save.

lessons.title: Using the AI Agent
lessons.description: Navigate the AI Agents area of GoHighLevel and understand what each tab is used for, from building managed agents to browsing prebuilt industry agents.
whatYouWillLearn: Open the AI Agents area from the left sidebar
Where to build and manage prompt based agents in Agent Studio
Where voice receptionists and Conversation AI agents are created
How knowledge bases and agent templates support your agents
Where AI generated text and images are tracked in Content AI
How to deploy a prebuilt agent from Industry Agents

sop.heading: Open AI Agents
steps: In the left sidebar, click **AI Agents**. The page opens on the **Getting Started** tab.

Review the tabs across the top: **Getting Started**, **Agent Studio**, **Voice AI**, **Conversation AI**, **Knowledge Base**, **Agent Templates**, **Content AI**, **Agent Logs** and **Industry Agents**.

sop.heading: Build and manage agents
steps: Click **Agent Studio** to see **Managed Agents**. These are prompt based agents that can use a prompt, knowledge, web search and integrations to analyze and build things inside the account. Click **Create Managed Agent** to start one, or **New Folder** to organize them.
Click **Voice AI** to set up an AI voice receptionist. Click **Create from scratch** to build one, or **Explore templates** to start from a template.

Click **Conversation AI** to manage agents that talk to leads for you. Click **Create Agent** to build one, or **Go to Agent List** to view existing agents. Use **Manage Knowledge Base** to control what the agent knows.
Click **Knowledge Base** to view the knowledge bases your agents draw from. Click **Create knowledge base** to add one.

sop.heading: Templates and content
steps: Click **Agent Templates** to browse ready made agent templates for conversations with leads. Use the filters on the left (**Categories**, **Use Cases**, **Business Niche**, **Pricing**, **Actions**) to narrow results. Each template shows whether it is **Free** or **Paid**.
Click **Content AI** to review AI generated content. Use the **Text** and **Image** tabs, and filter by **Social Planner**, **Blog**, **Funnel**, **Website**, **Email** or **Conversation**.
Use **Agent Logs** to review agent activity.

sop.heading: Use an industry agent
steps: Click **Industry Agents**. Under **My agents** you see agents already deployed in the account.
Under **Available agents**, review the preconfigured agents and click **Use this agent** on the one that fits, or click **Add industry agent** to add one.

Industry Agents: My agents at the top, Available agents with Use this agent below

lessons.title: Using Marketing Tools
lessons.description: Find your way around the Marketing area of GoHighLevel, including social posting, email campaigns, snippets, countdown timers, trigger links, ads and prospecting.
whatYouWillLearn: Connect social accounts in the Social Planner
Review email performance and start an email campaign
Where snippets, countdown timers and trigger links are managed
What trigger links do inside emails and SMS
Where to activate Ad Manager and add prospects

sop.heading: Open Marketing
steps: In the left sidebar, click **Marketing**. The tabs across the top are **Social Planner**, **Emails**, **Snippets**, **Countdown Timers**, **Trigger Links**, **Affiliate Manager**, **Brand Boards**, **Ad Manager** and **Prospecting**.

sop.heading: Social Planner
steps: On the **Social Planner** tab, under **Connect your social accounts**, click **+ Connect** below the network you want to link (for example **Facebook**, **Instagram**, **LinkedIn**, **TikTok**, **YouTube**, or under **Also available**, **Pinterest**, **Threads**, **Bluesky**, **GBP** or **Community**).
Once accounts are connected, use the Social Planner to schedule posts to them.

sop.heading: Email campaigns
steps: Click **Emails** to open **Email Marketing**. The **Statistics** tab shows the **Engagement summary** (Delivered, Opened, Clicked, Ordered) for your campaigns.
Use the **All Campaigns** dropdown and the date range to filter the statistics. Hover a bar to see the breakdown by campaign type.
Click **Create campaign** to build a new email campaign. Use the **Campaigns** and **Templates** tabs to manage existing campaigns and templates.
If the page shows **You're viewing sample data**, click **Clear sample data** to remove the demo numbers.

sop.heading: Snippets, timers and trigger links
steps: Click **Snippets** to manage saved message content. These are the same snippets available in Conversations. Click **New Snippet** to add one, or **New Folder** to organize them.
Click **Countdown Timers**, then click **New** to create a timer for an offer or deadline. The timer can be placed inside emails.

Click **Trigger Links**, then click **Add Link** to create a link. Place trigger links inside an email or SMS to track when a contact clicks and to trigger events based on that click. Use the **Analyze** tab to review link activity.

sop.heading: Other marketing tabs
steps: Click **Ad Manager**, then **Activate Ads Manager** to launch and manage ads across Facebook, Google and LinkedIn from one place.

Click **Prospecting** to open **Prospect accounts**. Click **Add prospect** to add a business and generate audit reports. The header shows how many premium reports remain this month; **Unlock premium** upgrades the feature.

**Affiliate Manager** (dropdown: **Dashboard**, **Campaign**, **Affiliate**, **Payout**, **Media**, **Settings**) and **Brand Boards** (**Design Kit**, **Brand Voice**) are also available in this area.

lessons.title: Understanding Automations
lessons.description: Learn how GoHighLevel workflows are built from a trigger and actions, create a simple workflow that adds new contacts to a pipeline, and keep workflows organized in folders.
whatYouWillLearn: Open the Workflows list and start a new workflow
Describe an automation to the built in AI
Name a workflow
Add a trigger and an action
Add new contacts to a pipeline stage automatically
Browse the available action categories
Create folders and move workflows into them

sop.heading: Start a workflow
steps: In the left sidebar, click **Automation**. The **Workflows** tab shows the **Workflows list**.
Click **Create workflow** (or **Build using AI**). The workflow builder opens on the **Builder** tab.
To have AI build it for you, type what you want in the **What do you want to automate?** box, for example: after sending a proposal, send an SMS follow up 24 hours later to confirm it was signed.
Click the workflow name at the top of the builder (pencil icon) and rename it so it is clear what the workflow does.

sop.heading: Add a trigger
steps: Click **Add new trigger**.
In the **Add trigger** panel, search for the trigger (for example type "new") and select **Contact created**.
Confirm **Choose a workflow trigger** shows **Contact created**, then click **Save trigger**.

sop.heading: Add an action
steps: Click the **+** below the trigger to open the **Actions** panel.
Search "opp" and select **Create/update opportunity**.
Set **In pipeline** (for example **Lead Pipeline**) and **In pipeline stage** (for example **New Lead**).
Leave **Opportunity name** and **Opportunity source** blank if not needed. If leads usually close at a set amount, enter it in **Opportunity value**.
Set **Status** to **open**, then click **Save action**. The workflow now adds every newly created contact to the selected pipeline stage.

To explore other actions, click **+** again and scroll the **Actions** panel. Categories include **Communication** (Send email, Send SMS), **Internal** (If / else, Wait), **Opportunity**, **Payments**, **Workflow AI**, **External AI models** (GPT powered by OpenAI) and marketing actions such as **Meta conversion API**. The **Apps** tab holds integrations.

sop.heading: Organize workflows in folders
steps: Return to the **Workflows list** and click **Create folder**.
Enter a **Folder name** and click **Create**.
Tick the checkboxes next to the workflows that belong in the folder, then click **Move** in the toolbar.
In the **Move items to folder** window, pick the folder (or click **New folder**) and click **Move Here**.

importantNotes: The builder shows a **Draft** / **Publish** toggle at the top right. The video does not show publishing; the demo workflow stayed in Draft.

lessons.title: Using the Sites Tab
lessons.description: Find your way around the Sites area of GoHighLevel, understand what each tab is used for, and start a new funnel from scratch, with AI, or from a template.
whatYouWillLearn: Open the Sites area and move between its tabs
Understand the difference between a funnel and a website
Know where to build stores, blogs, forms, surveys, chat widgets and QR codes
Find the Client Portal dashboard, settings and branded app options
Start a new funnel from blank, with AI, or from a template

sop.heading: Open the Sites area
steps: In the left sidebar, click **Sites**. The **Funnels** tab opens by default.

Use the tab bar across the top to switch tools: **Funnels**, **Websites**, **Stores**, **Webinars**, **Analytics**, **Blogs**, **WordPress**, **Client Portal**, **Forms**, **Surveys**, **Quizzes**, **Chat Widget** and **QR Codes**.

sop.heading: Know what each tab is for
steps: Use **Funnels** for pages that lead a visitor to one specific action, such as booking an appointment.
Use **Websites** for general information pages about the business.
Click **Stores** to build an online store. The first visit shows **Welcome to Stores!** with a **Start Onboarding** button; after that, use **New store**.
Use **Webinars** to build webinar funnels and **Analytics** to review site performance.
Click **Blogs** to manage blogs. Use **Create blog** or **New blog site** to add one.
Hover over **Client Portal** to open its menu: **Dashboard**, **Settings** and **Branded Mobile App**. Use these to review and brand your client portal.

Click **Forms** and then **Create form** to build a form with the drag and drop builder. Click **Surveys** and then **Create survey** to build a survey the same way. Add finished forms and surveys to your website pages.
Click **Chat Widget** and then **New** to create a chat widget, then add it to your website.
Click **QR Codes** to create QR codes.

sop.heading: Start a new funnel
steps: On the **Funnels** tab, click **New funnel**. (You can also click **Build with AI** directly.)
In the **Create new funnel** window, choose how to start: **From blank** (enter a **Funnel name**), **Build with AI**, or **From templates** to pick from the prebuilt template library.
Click **Continue**.

screenshots.caption: The Sites tab bar, with the Client Portal menu open showing Dashboard, Settings and Branded Mobile App.
The Create new funnel window: start From blank, Build with AI, or From templates, then click Continue.

lessons.title: Connecting Your Profile & Calendar
lessons.description: Update your user profile, connect a third-party calendar, set your weekly availability, and configure notifications and your password from My Profile.
whatYouWillLearn: Open My Profile from Settings
Update your personal details and email signature
Start a third-party calendar connection
Set weekly working hours and date-specific overrides
Choose how you receive notifications
Change your password

sop.heading: Open your profile
steps: In the left sidebar, click **Settings**.
Click **My Profile**.

sop.heading: Update personal details
steps: On the **General** tab, under **Personal Details**, update **First Name**, **Last Name**, **Email**, **Phone** and **Extension**. Upload a **Profile image** if needed (512 x 512 px, no bigger than 2.5 MB).
Under **Signature**, write your email signature in the editor. Turn on **Enable signature on all outgoing messages** and, if wanted, check **Include this signature before quoted text in replies**.
Click **Update profile**.

sop.heading: Connect your calendar
steps: Click **Calendar** in the profile menu. The **Calendars** tab shows your **Connected calendars**.
Click **Add new** to connect a third-party calendar so bookings sync and your availability is checked against it.

Under **Additional calendar settings**, leave **Hide event details** on for **Private mode for synced events** so only you can see third-party event details, and choose a **Timezone** under **View appointments in**.

sop.heading: Set your availability
steps: Scroll down to the weekly hours. Check each day you are available; leave a day unchecked to mark it **Unavailable**.
For each checked day, set the **Start time** and **End time** with AM or PM. Use the icons beside the row to add another time range, delete a range or copy the hours.
To override weekly hours on specific dates, click **Add date specific hours** under **Date specific hours**.

sop.heading: Notifications and password
steps: Click **Notifications**. Under **Notification Settings**, choose the channels (**In-App**, **Email**, **SMS**) and expand each category, such as **Conversation Notifications**, **Task Notifications** and **Calendar Notifications**, to set what you receive. Click **Save**.
Click **Security** to change your password. Enter **Current password**, **New password** and **Confirm password**, then click **Update password**.

importantNotes: The calendar connection flow after clicking **Add new** is not shown in the video. Follow the on-screen prompts for your calendar provider.

screenshots.caption: My Profile > Calendar: the Add new button under Connected calendars and the Additional calendar settings.
Weekly hours with Start time and End time per day, and the Add date specific hours button.

lessons.title: Creating a Calendar
lessons.description: Create a new booking calendar in Settings and share its booking link, and know where the other Business Services settings (email, phone, WhatsApp) live.
whatYouWillLearn: Open calendar settings from Business Services
Choose the right calendar type
Set the calendar name, description, team member, URL, and meeting duration
Find advanced settings for availability
Copy a calendar's scheduling or permanent link to share
Locate Email Services, Phone System, and WhatsApp settings

sop.heading: Create a calendar
steps: Click **Settings** at the bottom of the left sidebar, then under **BUSINESS SERVICES** click **Calendars**. The **Calendars** list opens on the **Meetings** tab.
Click **New calendar**.

In **Choose calendar type**, select the type you need: **Personal booking** (one-on-one with a specific team member), **Round robin** (rotates appointments among team members), **Class booking** (one host, multiple participants), or **Collective booking** (multiple hosts, one participant). Click **Explore more types** for other options.
In the **New calendar** window, enter the **Calendar name**. Click **Add description** to add a description.
Under **Select team member**, confirm or choose the team member the calendar belongs to.
In **Custom URL**, enter the URL slug for the booking page (for example my-calendar).
Set **Meeting duration** and choose the unit (for example **Minutes**).
Review **Booking availability**. To customize hours and other options, click **Advanced settings**.
Click **Confirm** to create the calendar.

sop.heading: Share a calendar
steps: In the calendar list, find the calendar and click the share (arrow) icon in the **Actions** column.

In **Share calendar**, on the **Scheduling link** tab, click **Copy** next to **Scheduling link** or **Permanent link** and send it to the person booking. Use the **One time link** or **Embed code** tabs for those options.

sop.heading: Other Business Services settings
steps: Click **Email Services** to manage your sending domain. Use **Add a dedicated domain** or **Dedicated Domain And IP** to connect your own domain for higher sending limits and better deliverability.

Click **Phone System** to get and manage phone numbers and complete A2P registration, using the **Phone numbers**, **Regulatory Bundles**, **Messaging**, **Voice**, **Trust Center**, and **Additional Settings** tabs.
Click **WhatsApp** to set up WhatsApp messaging if you use it.

importantNotes: The Scheduling link changes if you change the calendar's URL slug. Use the Permanent link for funnels, website redirects, and ads, since it stays the same.
Text messages cannot be sent from a phone number until it is registered for A2P.

screenshots.caption: Choose calendar type: Personal booking, Round robin, Class booking, or Collective booking.
The New calendar window with name, team member, Custom URL, meeting duration, availability, and Advanced settings.
Share calendar: copy the Scheduling link or the Permanent link.

lessons.title: Creating Custom Fields & Custom Values
lessons.description: Create custom fields to store data GoHighLevel does not track by default, and create custom values that insert saved text into messages and emails.
whatYouWillLearn: Open the Custom Fields and Custom Values pages in Settings
Choose the right field type, such as dropdown, file upload or date picker
Attach a field to the Contact, Opportunity or Business object and a folder
Add dropdown options and create the field
Understand what a custom value is and how to add one

sop.heading: Create a custom field
steps: Go to **Settings** and click **Custom Fields** in the settings menu.
Click **Create field**. The **Create custom field** panel opens.

Open the **Field type** dropdown and choose the type you need, for example **Single line**, **Number**, **Dropdown (single)**, **Dropdown (multiple)**, **Radio select**, **Checkbox**, **File upload** or **Date picker**.
Open **Add to object** and choose where the field will appear: **Contact** (contact record), **Opportunity** (opportunity card) or **Business**.
Open **Folder name** and choose the folder the field belongs in.
Enter the **Field name**, for example a question such as "Are you located in the area?". The **Key** is generated automatically.
For a dropdown field, type the first choice in **Enter option** under **Dropdown options**, then click **Add option** and enter each additional choice (for example Yes and No).
Check the **Live preview** on the right, then click **Create custom field** to save.

sop.heading: Create a custom value
steps: In the settings menu, click **Custom Values**.
Click **Add custom value**.
Enter a **Name** for the value (for example Facebook) and the **Value** it should insert (for example the business Facebook URL). Optionally choose a **Folder**.
Click **Create**. Insert the custom value in a text message or email and it fills in the saved value automatically.

importantNotes: Select **Add to object** and **Folder name** before entering dropdown options or other details. The trainer warns that changing these afterward clears the options you already entered.
Use custom fields only for data that does not already have a standard field in the CRM.

screenshots.caption: Add to object options: Contact, Opportunity and Business.
A dropdown field with its name, auto-generated key, two options and the live preview. Object and folder still need to be selected before Create custom field is enabled.
The Add custom value window with Name, Value and Folder.

lessons.title: App Marketplace & Reporting
lessons.description: Get oriented with the remaining sidebar tools: Memberships, Media Storage, Reputation, Reporting and the App Marketplace, and know what each is used for.
whatYouWillLearn: Where courses and communities live under Memberships
Where uploaded images and videos are stored
How to reach the Reputation dashboard for reviews
How to open call, appointment and ad reports
How to generate a Local Marketing Audit
How to browse and search the App Marketplace

sop.heading: Memberships, Media Storage and Reputation
steps: In the left sidebar, click **Memberships** to build courses and communities. Use the tabs at the top: **Client Portal**, **Courses**, **Communities** and **Credentials**.
Click **Media Storage** to see every image and video uploaded to the account. Use **Upload** to add files, or **Connect Canva** and **Connect Drive** to link those sources.
Click **Reputation** to track and manage reviews. On the **Overview** tab, use the **Get Started** checklist (starting with **Connect Google Business Profile**) to connect your Google reviews.

sop.heading: Reporting
steps: Click **Reporting** in the left sidebar.
Click **Google Ads** or **Meta Ads (Facebook Ads) report** to view ad reporting once those accounts are connected.
Click **Call report** to review call activity. Switch between **Incoming** and **Outgoing**, and adjust the date range as needed.
Click **Appointment report** to see appointments by status (Booked, Confirmed, Cancelled, Showed, No-show and more).
Click **Local Marketing Audit** and then **Generate report now** to create an audit of website performance, local SEO and local search rankings.

sop.heading: App Marketplace
steps: Click **App Marketplace** in the left sidebar to open **Marketplace Apps**.
On the **All Apps** tab, use **Search Apps** or the filters on the left (**Categories**, **Business Niche**, **Pricing** and others) to find apps for your industry, such as Canva or Slack.
Check **Installed Apps** to see what is already added to the account.

Marketplace Apps with the Search Apps box and filters on the left.
